content.title: Connection Without Losing Yourself
content.scope: A Little More Room · Eight brief educational readings, with optional everyday practices. These are not diagnosis or treatment.

intent.subject: Connection Without Losing Yourself
intent.direction: Explore a practical psychological perspective with ordinary examples and realistic limits.
intent.perspective: Public education; gentle, optional practices without clinical promises.

readings.label: Connection can include limits
readings.text: Connection does not mean being available to everyone. A supportive relationship can include honest requests and clear limits. Today, we will explore a small way to ask for company without losing your own needs.
readings.learn: Connection does not mean being available to everyone. A supportive relationship can include honest requests and clear limits. Today, we will explore a small way to ask for company without losing your own needs.

readings.label: Name the kind of support
readings.text: Do you want listening, practical help, advice, or simply company? These are different requests. Naming the kind of support gives the other person a clearer opportunity to understand what you need.
readings.learn: Do you want listening, practical help, advice, or simply company? These are different requests. Naming the kind of support gives the other person a clearer opportunity to understand what you need.

readings.label: Choose a suitable person
readings.text: Different people can offer different things. A friend may be a good listener; a group may offer shared interests. A professional can provide another kind of support. One person need not fill every role.
readings.learn: Different people can offer different things. A friend may be a good listener; a group may offer shared interests. A professional can provide another kind of support. One person need not fill every role.

readings.label: Make a specific invitation
readings.text: Try a small invitation: would you have ten minutes to listen later? You can add, I am not looking for solutions right now. A clear request is more useful than expecting someone to guess.
readings.learn: Try a small invitation: would you have ten minutes to listen later? You can add, I am not looking for solutions right now. A clear request is more useful than expecting someone to guess.

readings.label: State a limit you can keep
readings.text: A boundary might sound like: I cannot talk tonight, but tomorrow afternoon could work. Describe your own availability and choices. A limit is not a guarantee that another person will respond as you hope.
readings.learn: A boundary might sound like: I cannot talk tonight, but tomorrow afternoon could work. Describe your own availability and choices. A limit is not a guarantee that another person will respond as you hope.

readings.label: Leave room for their answer
readings.text: The other person may not have capacity today. That can disappoint you without defining your worth. You can suggest another time or look for another source of support, while respecting their answer.

readings.label: Build more than one connection
readings.text: A shared-interest group, a reliable friend, or a community activity can become part of a wider support map. Start with one realistic possibility. Belonging does not require being outgoing in every setting.

readings.label: Safety comes before reconciliation
readings.text: Pressure, threats, or abuse call for appropriate support, not better performance at communicating. Choose safety over reconciliation when needed. These ideas are educational; seek qualified help when a situation or persistent distress needs more support.
